newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa spikes higher on late fund covering.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa spikes higher on late fund covering.

text.p: A sudden late rally driven by fund short covering swept London cocoa futures higher by the close on Thursday, lifting them above the 950 stg barrier basis March.

Traders said the rally was likely to have been inspired by currency-related factors. Funds taking views on sterling might have decided that it was vulnerable to further losses despite a bounce from lows early on against the dollar and mark.
"People are still concerned about how far it can drop," said one trader.
The last-minute rally secured a technically-encouraging close of one-month high of 952 stg a tonne on March, up 19 stg on the day, although it was off the day's peak of 954 stg.
An earlier push this week had stalled at 950 stg and traders considered this level as a psychological resistance.
But despite the gains, which ranged between eight 19 stg on other contracts, traders reckoned the market would run into profit taking or origin selling in the absence of constructive industry buying.
"Industry are not going to be frightened by this move," said one. "It's just purely a technical move and it will be difficult to sustain it," he said.
Resistance for March is pegged at a chart gap between 954 and 956, followed by 968 stg.
Turnover totalled 7,113 lots with March/May switches exchanged at 19 stg. Some origin selling was cited in forward positions such as May and July.
London saw extensive support from arbitrage deals which favoured sterling-denominated business against New York.

In other news, shipments from Ivory Coast's Abidjan and San Pedro ports are estimated to have risen to around 120,000 tonnes by end-November. Official statistics for October and November are not yet available.
